summary: Close a four-species absorbed-power ledger into source-ordered percentage shares, failing closed when the derived total is zero instead of emitting an undefined split.

identity.relation: four-species absorbed-power ledger to source-ordered percentage shares and the closure residual
identity.direction: species_power_values -> total_power, species_fraction_percent, total_fraction_percent, fraction_sum_residual_percent, branch
identity.definition: Sum the four ledger entries in caller order, divide each entry by that sum and scale by one hundred, then report the sum of the resulting percentages and its residual against one hundred percent.
identity.model: source-defined absorbed-power split across exactly four species
identity.geometry: not applicable; the relation is a per-ledger scalar closure with no spatial dependence
identity.coordinates: not applicable; entries are carried in the caller's species order and never reordered
identity.boundary: the derived total is required to be finite and exactly non-zero; a zero total is rejected rather than approximated
assumptions: The four entries are the absorbed powers of one source-defined species ordering; the operator never infers or reorders species.
A negative entry is a physically meaningful signed contribution and is reported as computed, not clipped.
The relation is the same for both observed source routes: the E-star-dot-J route and the Wdot route differ only in the entry-point name.

inputs.name: species_power_values
inputs.description: Absorbed-power ledger in source-defined species order.
inputs.constraints: Exactly four entries; real-valued, non-boolean, non-string, and finite. Complex, boolean, string, or object entries are rejected.

outputs.name: total_power
outputs.description: Sum of the four ledger entries in the same units as the input.
outputs.constraints: Finite and non-zero; the call is rejected otherwise.

outputs.name: species_fraction_percent
outputs.description: Percentage share of each species, in the caller's species order.
outputs.constraints: Entry i equals 100 * value_i / total_power; entries may be negative when the corresponding ledger entry is negative.

outputs.name: total_fraction_percent
outputs.description: Sum of the returned percentage shares.
outputs.constraints: Reported as computed; it is close to but not exactly 100.0 in floating point.

outputs.name: fraction_sum_residual_percent
outputs.description: Closure residual, equal to total_fraction_percent minus 100.0.
outputs.constraints: Exactly the difference of the two reported values, not an independently recomputed quantity.

outputs.name: branch
outputs.constraints: Always the literal 'nonzero_total'; the zero-total branch is not represented as a value because it is rejected.

preconditions: The four entries belong to one source-defined species ordering.
The caller has already established that the ledger total is physically meaningful.
supported: Positive ledgers, single-species ledgers, and ledgers with negative entries.
Ledgers whose total is small but non-zero.
excluded: Ledgers whose total is exactly zero, for which the source defines no percentage result.
Ledgers with fewer or more than four species.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when the ledger is not a length-four vector, is complex, boolean, or string typed, contains non-finite entries, or cannot be converted to float; and when the derived total is non-finite or exactly zero.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: No runtime failure path beyond input validation; the arithmetic is a fixed number of NumPy reductions.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this operator has no iteration or feedback.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected ledger produces no mapping.

provenance.lineage_summary: SciRel-owned merge of two source routes that implement the same four-species absorption closure: the E-star-dot-J route and the Wdot route. The observed implementations differ only in the entry-point name and docstring wording, so SciRel carries one scientific identity with both routes recorded here as provenance. The observation snapshot and the batch inventory are private review artifacts and are not part of the public contract.

example.description: Close a four-species ledger and show that a zero-total ledger is rejected rather than split.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.diagnostics import compute_species_absorption_fraction
result = compute_species_absorption_fraction([1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0])
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['species_fraction_percent'], [10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0])
assert result['total_power'] == 10.0
assert result['branch'] == 'nonzero_total'
assert abs(result['fraction_sum_residual_percent']) < 1e-12
try:
    compute_species_absorption_fraction([0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('a zero-total ledger must be rejected')
example.expected: A mapping with the four species shares in caller order and a zero-total ledger that raises ValueError.

scope: Exact reproduction of both observed source routes on identical ledgers, including the returned keys and array values.
Source ordering of the returned shares and closure to one hundred percent.
Single-species ledgers, negative ledgers, and small-total ledgers.
Fail-closed behavior at the exact zero-total boundary and under signed cancellation.
Fail-closed validation of ledger length, dtype, and finiteness.
Exposure of exactly one public callable after the merge.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Establishes that the merged relation reproduces both observed routes on the tested ledgers and that the zero-total boundary fails closed. It does not establish that the four supplied powers are the correct physical absorbed powers for any particular run.
known_limitations: The species count is fixed at four; no general-length ledger is supported.
The zero-total branch is unavailable by design, so a physically zero-absorption run cannot be represented.
The observed aorsa3d source has been withdrawn from the current qualified D1 delivery pending whole-source re-review; its retained bytes support only historical development comparison.
The observed-route comparison requires the read-only source checkout to be reachable; it is skipped rather than silently passed when it is not.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
